proposal.title: Channel faces on every routed application, one _meta segment, and the server GUI as a separate component
proposal.author: Giovanni Porcari

problem.p: Three application classes expose the same router on different channels: OpenApiApplication (REST and OpenAPI), McpOpenApiApplication (REST, OpenAPI and MCP) and McpApplication (MCP only). McpOpenApiApplication is the most common base, and its name is long.
Each class reserves its own path segments inside the application: _meta and mcp. The rule for what an application may name its own routes is not written anywhere.

The server application _server extends OpenApiApplication, so it has no MCP face. A browser interface for _server is being built on gramlot. If it lives in kajenn, gramlot becomes a required dependency of the core.

current.fact: RoutedApplication is BaseApplication plus the genro-routes RoutingClass. Its execute is the single execution point that REST, MCP, WSX and the KajennBus reach.
OpenApiApplication attaches _meta with schema_json, docs (Swagger UI) and index.

McpOpenApiApplication adds the MCP JSON-RPC face under the segment mcp (mcp_name_segment). The channel plugin decides visibility: the MCP face lists only entries declared for channel mcp, and an undeclared method is REST only.
McpApplication makes the whole application one JSON-RPC endpoint over an external RoutingClass, with no REST face.
A path matching WELL_KNOWN_PATTERN goes to the route the application declared for it in its class dict well_known. No segment inside the application is reserved for it.
The server mounts ServerApplication under _server when no declared application has that code.
After the well-known paths, the server demux picks an application by the first path segment only. A mount is always one segment.

list.item: The OpenAPI face and the MCP face move into RoutedApplication. Every application with routes has both, with no switch to turn them off.

The channel of a plain HTTP request is named api, short for OpenAPI, in place of rest: kajenn calls a method by path and describes it with OpenAPI, it is not REST. A route for both faces declares channel_channels="mcp,api". Under _meta every branch is named after its channel: api and mcp.

Every RoutedApplication plugs the channel plugin with default api: a route that declares no channel_channels answers only on api. A route meant for WSX or another channel declares it, for example channel_channels="api,wsx".
The channel plugin keeps deciding visibility. Turning MCP on everywhere exposes nothing that is not declared for channel mcp.
OpenApiApplication, McpOpenApiApplication and McpApplication are removed in the release that brings the faces, with no deprecated alias. No new class name is needed.
RoutedApplication takes no external RoutingClass: the parameters routing_class, module and api_name are gone. To expose a RoutingClass that already exists, an application class contains it.
The parameter docs="off" stays and turns off only the Swagger UI page _meta/api/docs. The OpenAPI face and _meta/api/schema_json stay.
BaseApplication stays for applications without routes: RemoteApplication and raw ASGI applications.

section.title: One reserved segment: _meta
section.p: Inside a RoutedApplication the only reserved segment is _meta. It holds the administrative routes of the application. Application routes are never under it: a route pippo is reached as /<app>/pippo over REST and as tool pippo over MCP.

row.cell: Application page with links to the channel descriptions
List of the MCP tools, readable without speaking MCP

section.p: The names mcp and api become free for application routes.
Discovery documents are not under _meta: an application declares its well-known URLs in a class dict, and the _well_known branch was removed (well-known-urls, 2026-11-02).

section.title: SpaConsole in kajenn-orchestra
section.p: SpaConsoleMcpApplication becomes a RoutedApplication. The routes of SpaConsole are declared for channel mcp, so the OpenAPI face refuses them. Its MCP client moves from /<mount>/ to /<mount>/_meta/mcp.

section.title: Server application: API in kajenn, GUI in its own repository

list.item: ServerApplication stays in kajenn and serves OpenAPI and MCP only. It gains MCP by inheriting from RoutedApplication. kajenn does not depend on gramlot.
The GUI is a component in the repository kajenn-serverapp-gui, which depends on kajenn and gramlot.
The recipe enables it on the server element: gui(gui_class=...). Without the element there is no GUI. The core never names the GUI package.
ServerApplication builds the component as gui_class(self) (dual relationship) and passes every request on ui/... to it. The component releases its resources in on_shutdown. The URL is /_server/ui/.
The GUI reads and writes only through the OpenAPI face of _server, like any other client.
The routes of an extension keep using attach_section(section, name) of the core.
The GUI pages of an extension register on the GUI component, only when the component exists. ServerApplication exposes the component, or None.
gramlot is an optional extra of the extension, for example kajenn-orchestra[gui].
Pages generated from the OpenAPI description of each section are a future direction. They are not designed here.

decision.question: Where do the REST/OpenAPI and MCP faces live?
decision.choice: Every routed application answers network calls on every channel; visibility stays with the channel plugin.

decision.question: Can an application turn the faces off?
decision.choice: A schema lists only routes already exposed; a switch would be code without a verified use.

decision.question: Which segments does the kernel reserve inside an application?

option.title: Every segment starting with an underscore

decision.choice: One segment for every administrative route; reserving every underscore name takes too much from the application.

decision.question: Does McpApplication stay?
decision.choice: A RoutedApplication with routes declared for channel mcp gives the same result.

decision.question: How do OpenApiApplication, McpOpenApiApplication and McpApplication go away?

option.title: Removed in the release that brings the faces

decision.choice: kajenn is still in the laboratory: no application runs it in production.

decision.question: How long do the old URLs _meta/schema_json and mcp answer?

option.title: A period fixed case by case

decision.choice: A public URL that changes keeps answering for a while; the length is decided case by case, as for every deprecation.

decision.question: Does RoutedApplication take an external RoutingClass through routing_class, module and api_name?
decision.choice: What a recipe or a hot add names is always an application class.

decision.question: Does the parameter docs="off" stay?

option.title: Removed: the Swagger UI page is always there
Kept, for the Swagger UI page only

decision.choice: It turns off the page, not the OpenAPI face nor the schema.

decision.question: What is the channel of a plain HTTP request called, and the branch of _meta that describes it?
decision.choice: kajenn is not REST: a route is a method called by path and described by OpenAPI. The channel is openapi, and api is its short name.

decision.question: On which channels does a route answer when it declares no channel_channels?
decision.choice: A route answers where it says it answers; api is the face every routed application has.

decision.question: How does a recipe enable the server GUI?

option.title: Optional import of the GUI package
A boolean flag on the server
A gui element on the server naming the class

decision.choice: The recipe names the class; the core holds neither a dependency nor the name of the GUI package.

decision.question: What is the class named by gui?

option.title: A component built by ServerApplication and called for ui/...

decision.choice: It works with any _server class and needs no mixin.

decision.question: How do extensions add GUI pages?

option.title: Register on the GUI component when present
A separate GUI package per extension
Pages generated from the REST description

decision.choice: Generated pages remain the direction for later.

decision.question: What is the attribute of the gui element called?

option.title: gui_class
option.p: class is a Python keyword; other elements use app_class and handler_class.

decision.choice: The same shape as app_class and handler_class.

list.item: Three URLs change: /<app>/_meta/schema_json becomes /<app>/_meta/api/schema_json, /<app>/_meta/docs becomes /<app>/_meta/api/docs, and /<app>/mcp becomes /<app>/_meta/mcp. The old URLs give the same answer as the new ones, with a Deprecation header and a log line, for a period fixed case by case, as for every deprecation. A redirect is not used: an MCP client posting JSON-RPC does not follow it.
MCP clients and links to the docs must be updated.
Every route declaring the channel rest declares api.
A route of a plain RoutedApplication called over WSX, or over the KajennBus with a channel other than api, answers 404 until it declares that channel.
Every routed application reserves _meta. A route named _meta must fail at registration.
ServerApplication gains an MCP face.

Every application built on OpenApiApplication, McpOpenApiApplication or McpApplication moves to RoutedApplication in the release that removes them. genropy-kajenn uses OpenApiApplication through GenropyProxyOpenApiApplication.
A recipe passing routing_class or module to an application is rewritten with an application class that contains the routing class.
kajenn-orchestra moves SpaConsoleMcpApplication and registers its pool pages on the GUI component.
